newsitem.title: FRANCE: Victims' group hits back at Carlos the Jackal.
newsitem.headline: Victims' group hits back at Carlos the Jackal.

text.p: A French group representing victims of extremist attacks hit back at guerrilla "Carlos the Jackal" on Thursday after he challenged the impartiality of the country's chief anti-terrorism investigator.

The Venezuelan and his lawyer on Monday questioned the independence of judge Jean-Louis Bruguiere. They said his links with victims' association SOS Attacks, a civil plaintiff in investigations against Carlos, were "too close given the congratulations which this association regularly extends (to Bruguiere) in the press".

"SOS Attacks is independent of all authorities, be they political or judicial," group president Francoise Rudetzki responded in a statement made available to Reuters before publication in the daily Liberation on Friday.
"Obviously, the association mobilises in favour of victims of terrorist attacks to prevent their being isolated or vulnerable," she said.

Bruguiere has pioneered briefings with members of SOS Attacks to keep victims and their relatives informed of his various anti-terrorist investigations, although such meetings have not involved cases concerning Carlos.
The judge, who is on leave, was unavailable for comment.

Carlos, 47, whose real name is Ilich Ramirez Sanchez, was the reputed mastermind of some of the most notorious terrorist attacks of the 1970s and 1980s, including the 1975 kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers in Vienna.

He has been held in La Sante jail in Paris since he was seized in Sudan in 1994 and brought to France. He is to go on trial on December 12 for the murder of two French counter-intelligence officers in 1975.
